claims.claim: The answer is real even though the subject modulates to the dominant; the only fugue of the 48 where a modulating subject gets a real answer (works because it is two-part).
Only two perfect cadences: D major (bars 12-13) and E minor (bars 41-42).
Until the final section the entries are grouped in pairs, each echoing the subject-answer relationship at different pitches (e-b, G-D, a-e, d-a).
Bars 20-38 are an exact interchanged repetition of bars 1-19 (apart from pitch adjustment in bar 29); form in three divisions 1-19, 20-38, 39-42.
Episode 3 = interchange of episode 1; episode 4 = interchange of episode 2, at different pitch.
All episodes use falling sequences on roots falling by fifths; chord changes every bar except bars 10 and 29 (two chords each).
Root progression by falling fifths is used in almost three-quarters of the 200+ episodes in the 48.
Episode chord series: Ep1 F#, b, E, a, D, G, D; Ep3 B, e, A, d, G, C, A; Ep2 A, D, G, C, E; Ep4 E, A, D, G, B.
Three key areas: exposition bars 1-5 (i, v), middle bars 5-38, final section bars 39-42 (tonic).
The last complete entry is bars 32-33 in iv; final section has only half-subject entries.
